about: Hand-written place lines from the April 2026 Suit AI spec (IDEAS_FROM_APRIL_SPEC.md section 4), re-checked 2026-09-25 claim by claim against the CURRENT sourced data (data/topics_lore.json facts, data/places.json). Each entry keeps the April text verbatim, a verdict per claim (supported = a sourced fact says it, quoted in 'by'; unverified = nothing in current data says it; contradicted = current data says otherwise), and at most one LINE: Elah's first-person impression built only from supported claims plus opinion. Unverified and contradicted claims never reach a line. core/place_flavour.py adds each line to its place's topic node as her opinion.

places.april: Corporate-owned system. Four megacorps each control a planet. UEE maintains a presence but the corps run the show. Heavily populated, well-patrolled in monitored space. The "civilized" part of the verse — relatively speaking. Jump points to Pyro, Magnus, Terra, and Nyx.
checks: four megacorps each control a planet
Each of Stanton's four planets is owned by a megacorporation.
the UEE sold the planets to the corps
The navjumper Toshi Aaron discovered Stanton, and the UEE later sold its planets to corporations.
jump points to Pyro, Magnus, Terra and Nyx
Stanton has jump points to Magnus, Nyx, Terra and Pyro.

line.text: Every planet in Stanton is owned by a megacorporation. I call it the civilised part of the verse, relatively speaking.

places.april: Lawless system. No permanent UEE presence. Controlled by various outlaw factions — Nine Tails, Headhunters, and worse. Dangerous but full of opportunities for those willing to risk it. Comm relay coverage is spotty to nonexistent. Six planets, most of them hostile. The system's star is unstable.
checks: No central authority governs Pyro; competing gangs rule ever-changing sectors of control.
Outlaw groups in Pyro include the Headhunters, Fire Rats, Rough and Ready, and XenoThreat.
current data lists Headhunters, Fire Rats, Rough and Ready, XenoThreat; the Nine Tails are Stanton's (Grim HEX)
Pyro has six planets: Pyro I, Monox, Bloom, Pyro IV, Pyro V and Terminus.
Pyro's star is a K-type flare star, also known as a variable star.

line.text: Pyro has no central authority and a star that flares. I keep a hand near the sidearm the whole time we are there.

places.april: Semi-lawless frontier system. Home to Levski, a former mining facility turned independent settlement. People's Alliance territory. Gateway between Stanton and Pyro. Quieter than Pyro but don't mistake quiet for safe. Jump points to Pyro and Castra.
checks: Nyx is unclaimed by the UEE.
Levski, a former mining facility turned free settlement
Levski is a free town grown from the old QV Planet Services mining facility on Delamar.
Levski was founded by the People's Alliance and remains its headquarters.
jump points to Pyro and Castra (and Stanton)
Nyx has jump points to Bremen, Castra, Odin, Pyro, Stanton, Tohil and Virgil.
Nyx has jump points to Bremen, Castra, Odin, Pyro, Stanton, Tohil and Virgil.

line.text: Nyx is unclaimed by the UEE, and quieter than Pyro. I would not mistake the quiet for safe.

places.april: Arid, polluted planet. Owned by Hurston Dynamics — weapons and munitions manufacturer. Corporate security is aggressive. The surface is scarred by strip mining. Heavy industry everywhere.
checks: Hurston is a Super-Earth planet in Stanton, owned by Hurston Dynamics.
Hurston Dynamics manufactures ship weapons and munitions, and refines antimatter.
Mining and manufacturing on Hurston have killed almost all of its indigenous life.
strip mining is the Hathor Group's, not Hurston's, in current data

line.text: Mining and manufacturing killed almost everything native on Hurston. I find the whole planet heavy going.

places.april: Hurston's tidally locked moon. One side bakes, the other freezes. Thin atmosphere. Not much out here except outposts and trouble.
checks: current data spells it Arial (places.json, topics_lore arial)
Arial's surface temperatures sit considerably above the boiling point.
tidally locked, the other side freezes
current data: mostly nitrogen and toxic
HDMS-Bezdek and HDMS-Lathan are mining outposts on Arial.

line.text: Arial runs hotter than boiling and the air is toxic. I would keep any stop there short.

places.april: Toxic atmosphere moon. Acidic rain, poor visibility. Mining operations dot the surface but it's not a place you want to spend time outside.
checks: Aberdeen's sulfur-rich atmosphere gives the moon a yellow tint.
HDMS-Norgaard and HDMS-Anderson are mining outposts on Aberdeen.
Aberdeen is known primarily as the home of the Klescher Rehabilitation Facility.

line.text: Aberdeen has sulfur in the air, a yellow sky and the Klescher prison. I would not linger outside.

places.april: Smog-covered moon with low visibility. Industrial outposts scattered across the surface. Common staging ground for facility operations near Hurston.
checks: current data: mostly nitrogen and toxic
HDMS-Hahn and HDMS-Perlman are mining outposts on Magda.
Magda's atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and toxic, so breathing equipment is required.

line.text: Magda's air is toxic, so the helmet stays on. Mining outposts and not much else, to my eye.

places.april: Small, rocky, cold moon. Minimal atmosphere. Quiet — sometimes too quiet.
checks: Breathing equipment is required for all surface activities on Ita.
current data: almost entirely nitrogen, with methane and carbon monoxide

line.text: Ita needs breathing gear for everything on the surface. Quiet, sometimes too quiet, in my book.

places.april: Gas giant. You can't land on it but the upper atmosphere hosts Orison, a floating city. Crusader Industries builds ships here — Starliners, Hercules, the works. Platform-based infrastructure.
checks: gas giant with Orison in its clouds
Crusader's landing zone is Orison, a city in the clouds.
Crusader Industries builds ships here, on platforms
Crusader is owned by Crusader Industries, which builds ships on platforms in its skies.
Crusader Industries builds the Hercules military transport and the Mercury Star Runner.

line.text: Crusader is a gas giant with a city in its clouds, and Crusader Industries builds ships up there. That suits me fine.

places.april: Icy moon with an asteroid belt. Popular for drug labs and illicit operations. Beautiful to look at, dangerous to linger.
checks: Yela has its own asteroid belt, home to many small locations of interest.
Yela's water-ice crust is said to reflect the cool, calculating character it is named after.
The outlaw station Grim HEX sits in Yela's asteroid belt.

line.text: Yela is ice with its own asteroid belt, and Grim HEX hides in it. Pretty to look at, and I would not linger.

places.april: Entirely urbanized planet — every square meter is developed. ArcCorp is a mega-corporation that builds fusion engines. Area 18 is the main landing zone. Dense, loud, crowded.
checks: ArcCorp is covered in layer after layer of factory, so building more is now impossible.
ArcCorp makes jump modules, quantum drives, spacecraft engines and industrial mining equipment.
Area18 is one of ArcCorp's main commercial ports for interplanetary traffic.

line.text: ArcCorp is factory on top of factory, with no room left to build. Dense and loud, to my taste.

places.april: ArcCorp's icy moon. Mining operations and outposts. Cold, remote, and largely ignored by ArcCorp corporate.
checks: Lyria's icy surface has dirty ice, active cryogeysers and cryovolcanoes.
Shubin runs several mining and processing facilities on Lyria.
current data has Shubin mining there

line.text: Lyria is dirty ice and cryogeysers, with Shubin mining out in the cold. Remote, as I see it.

places.april: Small, arid moon orbiting ArcCorp. Low gravity. Relatively quiet.
checks: Wala is a moon orbiting ArcCorp.
Wala has a barren surface with outcrops of geode-like minerals.

line.text: Wala is barren, with geode minerals and air too thin to breathe. Relatively quiet, to my mind.

places.april: Frozen planet. microTech manufactures mobiGlas devices and computing equipment here. New Babbage is the landing zone — clean, modern, cold. The planet's climate was supposed to be temperate but the terraforming went wrong.
checks: Temperatures on microTech generally sit well below zero, especially during severe snowstorms.
An early terraforming error left microTech far colder and harsher than first projected.
microTech makes personal computing devices like the mobiGlas, plus spacecraft computers and datapads.
New Babbage is the largest city on microTech and a major trading hub.

line.text: microTech came out far colder than projected after a terraforming error. I always dress for it.

places.april: microTech's volcanic moon. Active geology, interesting terrain. Research outposts.
checks: current data: too cold for surface activity without survival gear
Rayari Cantwell and Rayari McGrath research outposts are on Clio.
Clio is too cold for surface activity without environmental survival gear.

line.text: Clio is too cold to work without survival gear. Research outposts and a long walk, as I see it.

places.april: Small, icy moon. Not much here — a few outposts and a lot of nothing.
checks: Euterpe is the smallest of microTech's three moons.
Euterpe has vast frozen oceans and exposed ice sheets.

line.text: Euterpe is the smallest of microTech's moons, frozen ocean and ice. A lot of nothing, to my eye.

places.april: Hostile planet in the Pyro system. Extreme temperatures and radiation. Outlaw territory through and through.
checks: Pyro IV's atmosphere is toxic, and breathing equipment is required on the surface.
No central authority governs Pyro; competing gangs rule ever-changing sectors of control.

line.text: Pyro IV is a rocky protoplanet with toxic air, in lawless space. I would rather be somewhere else.

places.april: Pyro VI: Distant ice giant in the Pyro system. Remote, cold, and largely unexplored.
checks: Pyro VI is an ice giant
Terminus, Pyro VI, is barren and desolate, bombarded by Pyro's solar flares.
Terminus is extremely cold, and storms can drop daytime temperatures below minus 120 degrees Celsius.
current data lists settlements and Ruin Station

line.text: Terminus is barren and brutally cold, and the factions there feud. I would rather be almost anywhere else.

places.april: Pyro system body. Outlaw staging area. Don't expect a warm welcome.
checks: Checkmate is the headquarters of Rough and Ready, a group of outlaws.
Pyro II is nicknamed Monox for the carbon monoxide in its atmosphere.

line.text: Monox is named for the carbon monoxide in its air. I would not expect a warm welcome anywhere near it.

places.april: Hurston's primary landing zone. Industrial, grimy, corporate-controlled. The gates are a maze and the transit system is slow. But it has everything you need — shops, hangars, medical.
checks: Lorville is Hurston's planetary capital and primary spaceport.
Lorville is a company town Hurston Dynamics established for its employees on Hurston.
Lorville has a Central Business District, a Workers District, and six city gates on its perimeter.
Lorville is surrounded by a wall that dwarfs even decently sized ships.

line.text: Lorville is a company town behind a wall that dwarfs ships. Grimy and corporate, and I mean that plainly.

places.april: microTech's showcase city. Clean, white, modern. Commons area is pleasant if you like the cold. Good shops. Feels sterile compared to Lorville.
checks: New Babbage is the largest city on microTech and a major trading hub.
New Babbage includes The Commons, New Babbage Plaza, the Promenade and Aspire Grand.
Large public spaces in New Babbage are enclosed under domes against the freezing elements.

line.text: New Babbage keeps its public spaces under domes against the cold. Clean, and to me a little sterile next to Lorville.

places.april: Floating city in Crusader's upper atmosphere. Beautiful — platforms connected by shuttles. Crusader's shipyard is here. The views are something else. Slow to navigate.
checks: Orison is a network of large interconnected platforms floating in Crusader's atmosphere.
Providence is Orison's industrial platform, home to Crusader's shipyards.

line.text: Orison is platforms floating in the sky of Crusader, with the shipyards out on Providence. Slow to cross, and I forgive it.

places.april: Area 18: ArcCorp's main landing zone. Urban canyon surrounded by skyscrapers. Loud, dense, commercial. The kind of place where everything's for sale.
checks: Area18 is one of the main commercial ports for interplanetary traffic around ArcCorp.
the IO-North tower is in current data, not a canyon of them

line.text: Area18 is one of the big commercial ports of ArcCorp. Loud and dense, and I assume everything is for sale.

places.april: Orbital station above Hurston. Well-equipped — hangars, cargo decks, medical. Common staging point for operations around Hurston and its moons. Feels like a second home if you spend enough time in Hurston space.
checks: places.json: Everus Harbor, Manmade, parent Hurston, system Stanton
not in the sourced lore; the brochure file may say it, as marketing

line.text: Everus Harbor is the station above Hurston. Spend enough time in Hurston space and I suspect it feels like home.

places.april: Orbital station above microTech. Clean, efficient, well-maintained. microTech quality — everything works the way it should.
checks: places.json: Port Tressler, Manmade, parent microTech, system Stanton

line.text: Port Tressler is the station above microTech. Clean and efficient, or so it always seems to me.

places.april: Bajini Point: Orbital station above ArcCorp. Busy. Lots of traffic.
checks: current data spells it Baijini Point
places.json: Baijini Point, Manmade, parent ArcCorp, system Stanton

line.text: Baijini Point is the station above ArcCorp. Busy, with traffic everywhere, as far as I can tell.

places.april: Orbital station above Crusader. Gateway to Orison.
checks: Seraphim Station is a Rest and Relax station in the trade lanes above Crusader.
Seraphim Station replaced Port Olisar above Crusader.

line.text: Seraphim Station replaced Port Olisar above Crusader. Named for the old shuttle maker, and I rather like that.

places.april: GrimHEX: Pirate station carved into an asteroid near Yela. No questions asked. The kind of place where you check your corners and keep your hand near your sidearm.
checks: station in an asteroid near Yela
Grim HEX is a sealed station built into an asteroid orbiting Yela.
After the housing exchange officially closed, outlaws, pirates and criminals took Grim HEX over.
current data writes Grim HEX (GrimHEX kept as an alias)

line.text: Grim HEX is an asteroid station near Yela that the pirates took over. I check my corners there.

places.april: Independent settlement in Nyx. Former mining facility turned political refuge. People's Alliance territory. Has its own character — rough, self-reliant, suspicious of outsiders.
checks: Levski is a free town grown from the old QV Planet Services mining facility on Delamar.
Activists escaping the Messers found refuge in Delamar's vacated mining facility.
Levski was founded by the People's Alliance and remains its headquarters.
current data: Levski still accepts those who wish to live away from the UEE

line.text: Levski grew out of an old mining facility, and the People's Alliance still keeps its headquarters there. Rough and self-reliant, to me.

places.april: Gateway station in the Nyx system. Transition point between Nyx and Stanton.
checks: places.json: Nyx Gateway, Manmade, parent Pyro, system Pyro
gateways are named for the far side
On the Pyro side, Stanton Gateway sits in a dense nebula and debris field, making navigation treacherous.

line.text: Nyx Gateway is out in Pyro, named for the jump it leads to. The gateways always point at the far side, as I read them.

places.april: Gateway station on the Stanton side of the jump point. Where you catch your breath after coming in from Pyro or Nyx.
checks: On the Pyro side, Stanton Gateway sits in a dense nebula and debris field, making navigation treacherous.
places.json: Stanton Gateway, Manmade, parent Nyx, system Nyx

line.text: Stanton Gateway on the Pyro side sits in a nebula and a debris field. Mind the navigation, I would say.

places.april: Gateway station on the Pyro side. Last stop before lawless space — or first stop coming back.
checks: Pyro Gateway is a station by the jump point from Stanton to Pyro, the port of entry between them.
Pyro Gateway is a station by the jump point from Stanton to Pyro, the port of entry between them.
Hurston Dynamics owns Pyro Gateway and added its logos and a statue of Archibald Hurston.

line.text: Pyro Gateway is the station of Hurston Dynamics at the jump to Pyro, statue and all. To me it is the last stop before lawless space.

places.april: Pyro settlement. Cobbled together from salvage and desperation. Don't drink the water.
checks: places.json: Patch City, Manmade_VisibleOnInteraction, parent Pyro, system Pyro

line.text: Patch City is out in Pyro. I would not drink the water, and I would not ask why either.

places.april: Pyro system refueling station. Named either ironically or as a warning.
checks: Gaslight and Rat's Nest are stations at Pyro V's Lagrange points.
current data: Pyro V is only a low-yield refueling point

line.text: Gaslight sits at a Lagrange point of Pyro V. Named ironically or as a warning, and I have never decided which.

places.april: Abandoned station in Pyro. Contested space. Scavengers, outlaws, and the occasional explorer. If the walls could talk, they'd probably scream.
checks: Ruin Station is an outlaw station orbiting Terminus in the Pyro system.
Ruin Station is an outlaw station orbiting Terminus in the Pyro system.
XenoThreat is listed as the pack controlling Ruin Station, but that may change at a moment's notice.

line.text: Ruin Station orbits Terminus and the outlaws run it. If the walls could talk, I suspect they would scream.

places.april: Automated rest stops at Lagrange points. Fuel, basic shops, medical, hangars. Utilitarian. Every system has them — they're the gas stations of space.
checks: a category, not a place in places.json: dropped
